title: A Component tool places a component from the tool bar
goal: The UI design mock puts a Component tool in the tool bar right after Frame: pick it, click or drag on the canvas, and a component from the library lands there. Photonz has no such tool yet, so the Design mode tool bar is one short of the mock and placing a component means dragging from the Library.
notes: Found finishing design-mode-puts-the-ui-tool-strip-in-the-tool-b (2026-10-09). Mock: docs/design/mocks/pages/ui-entry-wt.html tool strip id tComp, title "Component insert (C)", style color:var(--comp); UX-PATTERNS D4 UI design. Strip lives in WindowModes.designStrip (Sources/PhotonzCore/WindowMode.swift): add .tool(.component) after .tool(.frame) once the Tool case exists. Key conflict: Tool.shortcutKey gives C to crop/trim. Acceptance of the strip task says every tool keeps its key in every mode, so no mode-dependent C.
acceptance: A Component tool exists, sits between Frame and Shapes in the Design mode tool bar, and is drawn in the component colour as the mock draws it
Picking it and clicking the canvas places the component the Library has picked (or asks which one) at the click
It has a key that collides with no other tool (the mock says C, which is Crop here and in Photoshop; if C cannot be shared, the letter is a decision card)
Its row is under More and in Edit > Tools in every other mode, and a walk at Next defaults places a component with it by pointer

log.note: Adversarial review before building: (1) the mock's C is Crop here and in Photoshop, and the house rule is one letter per tool, so the letter goes to a decision card; N is free in Photoshop and in Photonz (the mocks give N to a prototyping Connect tool nobody has built). (2) 'asks which one': a click that answers with a question is clumsy, so the tool always places something: the Library's picked tile, else the one it placed last, else the first on the shelf, and the capsule over the bar names it before you click and swaps it (Photoshop's options bar habit). (3) The mock shows no click flow for the tool (its walkthrough drags from the Library), so placement reuses the Library drop path exactly: same landing rules, same linked copy, one undo step.

Built: Tool.component (key N, createsLayers, no colour capsule), ToolSetting.component, ComponentToolChoice (core, tested), ToolBarLayout.bar(withComponent:) at the end of the drawing family, Design strip Select | Frame, Component insert, Shapes, Pen, Text | Measure. App: violet ComponentGlyph button (white on the accent when in hand), capsule Picker over the Components shelf, canvas press places via placeComponent, Experiments.toolBarLayout is now the one place bar/More/Edit > Tools read. Tests: ComponentToolTests (14) + updated tool/strip tests; Scripts/test.sh 12045 pass. Walks: design-mode-tool-strip-walk (pointer click on the tool at Next defaults, places Button, capsule swaps to Card, places Card; 10 real captures), video-tool-bar-walk (Edit > Tools > Component insert), plus one-glass-tool-bar, tool-bar-fills-its-room, front-door, window-modes, design-ui-start, every-area-has-one-purpose all ok.

left rough (none clears the follow-up bar on its own; all are in the audit for the user to react to): a press places on the press, so dragging after it does not slide the new copy; no right hand panel section for the tool (the Library shelf is that place and picks the capsule too); More and Edit > Tools rows wear the system symbol the timeline's component track uses, since a menu row takes a system symbol.

Built and pushed (5ccaa34d): Component insert sits after Frame in the Design tool bar in the component violet, a pointer click picks it, a canvas click places the component the Library picked (else the last placed, else the first on the shelf) centred on the click, and the capsule over the bar names and swaps it; under More and in Edit > Tools elsewhere. Verified: 12045 tests, design-mode-tool-strip-walk and video-tool-bar-walk at Next defaults with real captures, audit 2026-10-09-component-tool. Waiting on one answer: the mock's C collides with Crop, so it ships on N and the letter is on a decision card (recommended: keep N).
